title: 滚妹人格｜属于我的蒙娜丽莎
text:
✎2431 
   ♥


这是我在看完RIDE/The Charlatans的Between Nowhere Tour以后在狂热状态下写的日记。
现在回想起来，那种快乐到眩晕的状态可能一辈子都不会再体验到了。因为疫情原因，在这场演出以前，我只看过校园乐队的小演出和没什么感觉的大团的arena演出。这是我第一次在这么近、这么小的场馆里看到水平很棒的、我很喜欢的乐队演出，身边还有亲密的朋友；RIDE的四个人带着他们的爆裂音响就这样杵在我面前，简直是根本不够看。第一次看到吉他手离我这么近地表演solo，那冲击力真是不一般。喝酒也没有经验，狂灌了一整瓶。费城Union Transfer的音量是我去过的场馆里最响的，当时我又不知道要戴耳塞，最后耳鸣了一晚上，然后拖着这个破听力和朋友躺在床上不停地反刍。那天还在下雪，当时我还是那种刚搬到北方的南方人，看到雪地还会兴奋，还没有开始讨厌冬天。
以后去看多著名的乐队或许都不会有这种感觉了，因为只属于我的蒙娜丽莎我早已遇见……

回巴尔的摩的火车真是太晃了。
度过了一个非常不错的周末！周五中午开完组会后和Ⰶ去学校里玩雪，玩了一个小时，然后乘Amtrak去了费城，在♫家和𓃝以及♫的室友一起吃了晚饭，她们做了腊肠饭，牛仔骨和虾饺，每个都好吃得离谱，非常满足。
18:45我们打车去了Union Transfer。整个下午我一直非常担心演出被取消，因为美国东北部在下暴风雪，我们大学的官方活动都被取消了。到达目的地以后，等的人已经在门口排成了一条长队，我就安心太多了，并且也很开心这么多人愿意提早一个小时过来。我们过了安检，买了酒，然后就跑到前排去等着了，心情简直就是飘飘欲仙的激动。





Union Transfer平面图


The Charlatans的部分我迅速带过。他们的主唱Tim Burgess巨会营业：当你还在为“我不是单纯来朝圣的，有5%的我是想在演出结束后发Instagram”而感到愧疚时，Tim已经在演出中间掏出手机号召大家挥手蹦迪，然后把手机倒过来拍自己了，网感未免有点太好。
中场休息时酒瓶已空。舞台的灯光是绿色的，我们站在第三排左侧的位置等着巡演工作人员把设备调好。我和朋友开玩笑说，待会儿可能就没有这么多营业了，因为Mark和Andy都有吉他在手上，腾不出手来指挥蹦迪。最先搬上来的是写着RIDE的底鼓，然后是三个效果器板，Steve的在左边，中间是Mark的，右边是Andy的。虽然完全不懂单块，一种强烈的瘙痒的冲动还是让我踮着脚努力去看板上到底有什么。伟大的建筑一般的电路系统啊。Mark有一个红色的块，上面的两行光点不停的来回闪动。吉他也搬出来了，两把Rickenbacker，一把樱桃红的，一把红色的；两把Gretsch，一把红的(其实是Trini Lopez)，一把原木色的。这时，音响里切到了Blur的The Narcissist。我忽然感觉这是我在The Ballad of Darren发行半年后第一次真正与这首歌共情。与朋友们微醺地站在台下等着喜爱的乐队上台的感觉如此之好，人生能有几次这样的经历呀？之前一直吐槽这首歌是Damon Albarn年近60终于把抑郁症治好了，现在只觉得幸福。可能是疫情的原因吧，身边的联系都显得愈发珍贵起来。





对耳膜宝具！


接着，灯光渐暗，音乐变成低沉而逐渐加快的鼓点。后台的灯光亮了起来，观众席里的嘈杂声落了下来，最后变成一阵阵的欢呼和尖叫。乐队成员上台了，我一边狂跳一边举着一个Love from China的牌牌，Mark问：大家好吗？准备好了吗？那就开始吧。
Seagull，狂风暴雨一般的嘶鸣声；Kaleidoscope，脑浆跟着吉他一起旋转；In a different place, 灯光似乎和音乐一起升腾；Polar bear, “如果云会唱歌，那就这就是它的声音”……
Dreams burn down开始之前，Mark逗观众一定要报出歌名才演，还一再嫌大家喊得不够响，一直努力保持矜持的我便再也无法忍受，发出了尖锐的爆鸣声。Loz的鼓太帅了。每一首歌都很完美。做实验的时候听的音乐，冬季闲逛看海时听的音乐，现在就在离我如此之近的舞台上，以这样暴力、直白、美丽的方式爆炸，震碎我的鼓膜直达灵魂。Vapour trail的前奏响起的时候我没有录像，而是百分百地投入合唱。音量如此之响，我基本聋了，听到Andy的声音是完全变形了的，但还是很开心。清新的旋律和单纯美丽的歌词，就像第一次点开Nowhere的那一刻一般，就像初恋一般。Tim给Here and Now合了口琴，我从未意识到口琴可以拥有这样近乎暴力的美感。然后是Nowhere, Lannoy Point, Monaco和新歌Peace Sign。前排的姐姐们应该是铁粉，在Peace Sign的副歌特别给面子地举起双手，比出“耶”的手势应援。收尾曲是Leave Them All Behind。前奏那段采样出来的时候我真的要哭了。Mark喝了一口他那蜂蜜威士忌，Andy看着笑一笑，Steve铺垫着前奏，然后两把Gretsch一起加进来。天呐，我离得那么近，近得可以看到每一个和弦变换和每一个推弦；所有的声音以一种迷幻又充满力量的方式在我脑后一块酸涩的区域混合起来。I don’t care about the colors, I don’t care about the light, I don’t care about the truth… 然后是吉他独奏——主旋律的变奏加上哇音踏板，音符跟着鼓点迸发出来，如此明亮，仿佛鸟儿沐浴着晨光从混沌的黑暗中挣扎而出。最后的outro是一浪高过一浪的音墙，就像刹车失效的公路旅行和不会有终点的逃亡……
接着魔法师停下了魔咒。Andy说，谢谢，希望我们能很快再见。 Loz给大家拍了照，我们在上面。
再接着就是长长的、似乎永远都不会结束的后劲。乘着这份飘飘欲仙的心情，我花了35刀买了丑丑的巡演T恤，在Union Transfer “sold out”的告示牌前面拍了照，在回♫家的出租车上跟着广播哼starman，最后变成大合唱；第二天幸福而无所顾忌地倒在费城美术馆前洁白松软的积雪上。
回到巴尔的摩后，真的感觉有变得更加热爱生活。我对♫说想把这一刻的幸福全部榨出来，风干储存，这样每次想回忆的时候就能掏出来看看，就又有力量可以继续生活了。我真的可以如此贪心吗？但至少到星期三的现在，坐在实验室的椅子上写这篇日记时，那种不可思议的快乐的心情依然存在。Maybe it’s really, really, really can happen!
再也吹不出那样的彩虹屁，看了也会红着脸躲避



  Kudos ♥

title: 滚妹人格｜夏日&盯鞋&音乐节初体验
text:
Slide Away
这个周末终于去了心心念念的Slide Away Festival。


’A genre that lends itself to loudness can still be overheard from its origins in the 1980s. Shoegaze, Dream Pop, Ambient, or whatever you may call it, has carried itself gracefully through decades while inspiring countless subgenres and infecting all walks of music along the way.
The audience reflects back the legacy and continued impact with a feeling of mutual admiration and respect is palpable across generations and identities - no matter the coast.
SLIDE AWAY is a celebration of the genre and all artists who shape sound in the most unique of ways, all the while bridging the gap between the diverse cast of boundary pushing mavericks of yesterday with the genre bending savants of now.’
——Slide Away官网的介绍

这是一个小有名气的美国盯鞋音乐节，24年开始办的，每年一届，一开始是为了庆祝费城和LA的盯鞋场景。主办方似乎是费城盯鞋乐队nothing。前几年的节其实我努努力应该也能去，但因为对领衔乐队的风格不怎么感冒所以搁置了。今年因为有Chapterhouse和Hum，并且开到了芝加哥，我就想，这次一定要去！于是去年九月份就买了票。
芝加哥的Slide Away开在uptown的Aragon Ballroom，场馆大小和DC的The Anthem （slowdive的演出场地）差不多。Uptown给人的感觉和费城的Fishtown很像，很有文艺的氛围，但也有点乱乱的。6点多进门，观众很礼貌，气氛很热烈。因为准备晚上开夜车回去，不能喝酒，所以我们只能喝无酒精饮料。芝加哥物价太贵，最后我们都喝了水。纯纯的白开水，装在啤酒瓶里，取了个唬人的名字叫Liquid Death……就这样无痛融入了喝酒的人群！
看下来最喜欢的居然是第二个表演的芝加哥小乐队sunshy，他们很年轻，24年才发第一张专辑。现场听起来音效极棒，旋律也写得有意思，对比之下其他乐队甚至都有点黯然失色。表演结束后我们立刻去周边摊买了T恤和场刊（对，他们甚至做了一本场刊），翻开发现居然是简体中文字。采访里主创说不想做90s乐队的单纯模仿者，想融合自己喜欢的其他流派和亚裔在美国的生活经验做新的东西。可能因为这样，他们才管自己的风格叫noise pop，而不是已经有点滥用的shoegaze吧！看得愈发喜欢，遂又回去排了队买了cd。同来的朋友有爱听国盯的，发现专辑附赠的小卡上有他最喜欢的乐队之一天然味道；后来发现他们都签在长沙/深圳的独立厂牌小动物唱片旗下。回家仔细听了专辑，真好听，颇有一些10年代国盯之风，清新诗意带点忧郁。最喜欢的曲子是On the train。邂逅喜欢的乐队的感觉真好，可能这就是音乐节的意义吧！





sunshy表演中。我们还遇到了一位乐队成员的妈妈。


无端联想：我很喜欢的观鸟博主竹雈在有一期记录一年内开过的公路的视频里用了Alcest的Souvenirs D’un Autre Monde做背景音乐，就说盯鞋和这种滚滚前进的意象很配吧！
Chapterhouse的表演不错。之前网友总跟我说他们和RIDE是异父异母的亲兄弟，确实能听出来相似之处：旋律是英国乐队一贯的明亮动听，很有pop感；节奏组很强劲，有几首歌有点舞曲味儿。就是人声听起来很苍老了。不过毕竟是老头了，这也是没办法的事。鼓手玩得很嗨，最后一直在一边打鼓一边指挥；主唱看起来头发特别茂密！





Chapterhouse


大多数美国人似乎都是为了压轴的Hum来的，Hum的周边售卖点排起了长队。但我们因为白天徒步了三个小时已经精疲力竭，还想留点体力安全驾驶打道回府，所以就早退了。事实证明这是一个正确的决策，朋友开的车出城回家，我在副驾驶上尽力保持清醒，已经到了出现幻觉的地步，觉得黑夜里有巨人在行走；而双手紧握着方向盘的朋友意志力已然达到超人级别。第二天都补了觉。下次一定！很想听到现场版的stars。
芝加哥的夜色真美，密歇根湖旁边的大道一看就是精心设计过的。我爱城市生活！

title: 滚妹人格｜夏日&盯鞋&音乐节初体验
text:
Total Bummer
30号去纽约找朋友玩，看了今年新开的另类摇滚音乐节Total Bummer。



和朋友们以emo teen的形态出击。是的这就是盯鞋爱好者。


音乐节所在的场馆Knockdown Center很有意思，是一个位于Brooklyn的废弃的玻璃/门框厂房，从Manhattan乘坐L线可达。场馆里有两个舞台，一个室内的main stage和一个室外的舞台the Ruins，乐队在这两个舞台上交替演出，基本不用在那干等换设备啥的；音效非常棒；场馆很大，通风透气，还有很多可以坐下来休息的地方，体验一级甲等。就是在室外的时候会吸到二手烟和麻，以及由于场馆实在太大了，找了一圈都找不到去周边售卖亭的路。非常神奇的是厕所里有attendant在递纸和兜售零食矿泉水。老天啊，难道我们没有别的更体面的挣小费方式了吗？





场馆非常工业风


由于下午先去吃了很好吃的格鲁吉亚菜Chama Mama，我们到得稍微晚了些。Teen Mortgage是个硬核朋克乐队，只有主唱、鼓手两人，但是依然在舞台上搞出了非常巨大的动静。Blonde Redhead是90年代的纽约乐队，曲风是实验/迷幻系的，鼓点的节奏很特别，主唱的姿态很美，挺喜欢的。回来还翻到了主唱Kazu和Lush的Miki的一个采访。Meat Puppets是来自凤凰城的乐队，风格非常美国。挤在抽着各种化学品的人群中看着晚霞在厂房上的反光、听着老头卖力弹琴，也蛮有情调。





在main stage演出的Dinosaur Jr


Dinosaur Jr的现场非常非常棒。久仰J Mascis华丽的吉他solo大名，现场听了，感受真是无比震撼。鼓和吉他都又强劲又稳，变化多端的旋律穿插着J懒洋洋的声音，非常适合随着音乐摇摆舞蹈……翻唱the Cure的Just Like Heaven和录音室版一样在第二段副歌戛然而止。老头们精力无限，6、7分钟的吉他solo演了一首又一首，人群随着音乐不停蹦跳摇晃，他们在远古时代肯定是非常厉害的萨满吧！

总之美丽的五月就这样结束了，又回到了我的中西部小农村过我的小日子>< 真是美好的回忆！

title: 书信｜妹亲启：高中生活完全不指南
text:
✎1774 
   ♥








21年给妹写的信，祝贺她考上高中。放在这里是因为忽然发现高中生活已经离我很远、很远了。



亲爱的妞妞：
生日快乐！祝贺你考上目标高中！
本来起草了一篇万字长信，后来一想，没有什么比生日时候收到一封啰啰嗦嗦自鸣得意的说教更扫兴了。于是我把想说的话浓缩成三点：

高中不仅仅是为高考做准备，打开视野，独立思考，尽情享受你的高中生活吧！
我的语文老师曾说，应试教育是手段，不是目的。鲜活的年轻生命都受不了枷锁，但带着镣铐努力跳完这一段舞，你能看到更广阔的天地。
心理健康很重要！必要时请向他人寻求帮助。

最后，再次祝你生日快乐！
渡鸦
P.S. 礼物说明
六月底的时候你说想要DND桌游，可惜我暂时没找到正版的，于是送你一套跑团骰子。常言道，扔骰子的意义在于你把它往天上一抛，就知道自己到底想选什么了！
还有一本是《房思琪的初恋乐园》，不知道你有没有看过。性犯罪比我们想象中的更频繁，千万警惕可能的骚扰行为！



那篇啰啰嗦嗦自鸣得意的说教

亲爱的妞妞：
15岁生日快乐！恭喜你升入理想的高中！
本来想写一篇万字长信，但回头一想，自己如果在生日当天收到一封洋洋自得的所谓“经验总结”，说不定白眼都要翻到天上去。不过分享欲是抑制不住的，如果你有兴趣的话烦请继续看下去啦！
我的母校XX中学以放浪不羁的校风闻名。受此影响，我认为高中的意义不仅仅是为高考厉兵秣马，更重要的是打开视野，审视自己，学会独立思考，为独立面对社会打下基础。即使不谈这些久远的意义，就谈高中，永远指望着抽象的目标奋斗也是不现实的。尤其是高三的时候，每天的重复劳动会让人怀疑人生，这时候抬头看看窗外像鸽子一样立在枝头的玉兰花，就觉得自己不仅仅是一台答题机器，而是站在这片土地上的一个人。
不过，既然选择了高考的道路，应试教育便是逃不过的话题。这一点上我并不是专家：我一直是兴趣驱动型的人，纯粹的奋斗不能让我感到快乐——上述的语文老师经常吼我“渡鸦，醒醒！”我能提供的有限经验和教训如下（应该也是老生常谈了）：首先，不要放弃任何一个知识点，尤其是理科，以后补起来得从地基开始补。老师脾气暴躁、阴阳怪气都不重要，不懂就问，不要因为和老师赌气就放弃自己的分数。然后，练习真的有用。高中知识都不会特别难，本质就是刷分，沉住气去练基本上都能练会。最后，成绩波动非常正常。我本人位比有从19%跳水到91%过，物理全卷只做对了三道题，数学十道填空错八道，都熬下来了，顶多关在厕所哭一会儿，找心理老师聊一会儿。
高中在我心里的另一个意义就是同学情谊。很幸运，我的班级氛围很好，我在这里认识了很铁有趣的朋友和许多非常欣赏的人，每天上课下课叽叽喳喳从火影忍者聊到感受态细菌和电磁场最后一大题，很开心。至于感情——我不知道你是不是这么想的，但我进高中时定下的目标就是：“要有最好的朋友，要有喜欢的人，要有爱好的学科和理想。”其他愿望基本实现，只有喜欢的人这一点以比较悲剧的方式结尾；教训是，如果感情强烈到了伤害自己的地步，最好找个人倾诉一番。无论如何，不要鄙视自己的感情；荷尔蒙会和青春年华一起在几年内迅速褪去，一切经历都是值得珍视的。
啰嗦到这里，我单独提一下老师。好老师对人的正面影响有多大不必多说。但也有素质不行的老师，从上课一直阴阳怪气贬低学生，到直接上手打上脚踢的都有。这时候不要怕，要知道他才是那个仗着一点权力就胡天胡地的垃圾，自己并不是犯错的那个；必要的情况可以寻求校方或者家长的帮助。并非不信任你的心理素质，只是我的一个高中同学被数学老师贬低到崩溃退学了，非常可惜。一定不能让自己的人生毁在这种人身上。关于性犯罪方面的问题，请参照生日礼物之一《房思琪的初恋乐园》（或许你已经看过）。
最后，再次祝你生日快乐！六月底的时候你说想要DND桌游，可惜我暂时没找到正版的，于是送你一套跑团骰子，以后遇到什么无法解决的难题，捏住两枚一扔就知道该选什么了～
送上我最喜欢的女诗人茨维塔耶娃诗一首：

“很快从燕子——变成女巫！ 青春！我们马上将告别…… 让我与你在风中小站片刻！ 我黝黑的青春！请安慰你的姐妹！
让紫红的裙子像火苗一般闪烁， 我的青春！我肤色黝黑的 小鸽子！我的灵魂的碎片！ 我的青春！安慰我，跳舞吧！
挥舞着天蓝色的纱巾， 喜怒无常的青春！我俩 尽情儿玩耍！跳吧，跳得热火朝天！ 别了，我金色的青春，琥珀的青春！
我不无用意地握起你的双手， 像告别情人一般与你告别。 从内心深处迸发出来的青春—— 我的青春！走吧，去找别人！ ”

渡鸦

title: Birding｜A Visit to Eagle Creek Park
text:
✎201 
   ♥


This weekend I visited Eagle Creek Park near Indianapolis with my friends. It’s freezing outside, so we only walked ~10 minutes on the trail, and saw some Canada geese, ducks, gulls, and coots on water from a distance. I could only identify Canada geese by their larger size compared to other birds >_<
To my surprise, the Ornithology Center at the Eagle Creek Park is really good. The ornithology center contains a wild birds rescue center (they’ve rescued a turkey vulture, a bald eagle, and a few owls), a little museum (a great collection of books, field guides, specimen, and memes), an indoor observation station facing the lake (helps a lot when it’s freezing outside, and you can borrow binoculars), and a few bird feeders (you can sit on chairs - indoor or outdoor - and watch birds enjoying their time, and don’t worry, there are anti-collision stickers on the windows). On the windows facing the trail, there are great window paintings - I really like the loon window, and hopefully I can see them during the spring/fall migration periods!
A very dedicated team curated everything. I pay due respect to all people working there, and we had a great time. Definitely want to visit there again in the future when it’s warmer!

text:
The Oregon Trail/俄勒冈之旅

美术：美丽｜剧情：不错｜玩法：有趣｜汉化：完美
评分：9/10




游戏的加载界面，绿色的牛车


完美的roguelite游戏，似乎是在游戏史上都赫赫有名的游戏老奶，一开始是做给80年代的美国小学生了解拓荒历史的。



游戏中最大的挑战之一：渡河


背景是美国19世纪的西部大拓荒，核心玩法是选择四个队友徒步踏上从密苏里州到俄勒冈州的“俄勒冈小径”，一路上要平衡队友的健康、卫生、士气等数值，并面对痢疾、霍乱、步枪走火、蛇咬等随机出现的挑战，食物主要靠打猎和钓鱼获得。作为一个已经把明日方舟当成集成战略启动器的人来说这实在太上头了。除了分为五段的主线任务“俄勒冈小径”以外还有各种钓鱼打猎的小挑战可选，也有支线任务“加利福尼亚小径”等等，但玩了一圈还是感觉主线任务最好玩，其他的有点太简单了，比较无聊。



卫生太低的话角色就会死于痢疾，这已经成为了一个梗


打完任务可以收集成就解锁各种俄勒冈小径的科普小故事。24年发布的这个版本有咨询原住民，所以里面有很多原住民相关的内容，按照reddit上面的讨论是有“makes it less racist”，毕竟白人的拓荒之旅就是原住民的受压迫史呢……

可以给NPC讲述你听到的故事，并观察故事在流传途中发生的变化


玩下来感觉像个美国众神的同人游戏。玩法几近于无，不过美术和音乐还是可以的，剧情比较零散，背景设置在上世纪大萧条时代的美国。主要玩法就是操纵主角走来走去然后点击地图上的故事图标聆听，加入了塔罗占卜的元素。作为一个还是喜欢玩“好玩的游戏”的人来说，这点剧情和美术还是没法支持我一直玩下去……



核心玩法就是变成一个骷髅一直走。可以搭乘顺风车或者火车，但走得也很慢，这一点上十分还原了


很不满的地方在于马里兰州没有故事，我所在的印第安纳州也没有故事！拜托！美国人做的游戏诶。所以我果然还是没有体验到美国的*核心生活*吗？

title: Birding｜Summertime: Watching Songbirds in Your Favourite Park
text:
✎1251 
   ♥
Summer has come - almost.
In western Indiana, it means the sun stays up until around 21:00, which makes it a very good time of year to watch songbirds after work.
My boyfriend sent me a pic of a scarlet tanager (‘black-winged redbird’, as he named it) on a tree which he randomly encountered on his way to work, and it left me green with envy. As a result, I started going birdwatching from 17:00 to 19:00. My target life list this summer includes the colorful songbirds specific to America - scarlet tanager, summer tanager, indigo bunting, and Baltimore oriole. Luckily, I’ve ticked off half my list in only three days.
crumbs: Birding｜Summertime: Watching Songbirds in Your Favourite Park

title: Birding｜Summertime: Watching Songbirds in Your Favourite Park
section: A Beginner’s Guide to Spotting Songbirds
text:
A Beginner’s Guide to Spotting Songbirds
Since I could always somehow find a place near water to live, I mainly watched shorebirds and waterfowl in the past; and since those birds can swim (obviously), they are much more bolder, thus easier to spot than songbirds. However, I don’t really want to go near water during summer - I don’t want to be a walking buffet for mosquitoes.
As a result, I started spotting songbirds, and had slowly gathered some tips over these days.

1. Birds are more likely to live on ‘edges’.
For some reasons I wasn’t sure enough, you can always see more songbirds at trailside compared to some place deep in the forest. Maybe it’s because there is more food.


2. Birds have their territories.
If you (or your Merlin bird ID app) hear a bird near a tree, and you can’t find them immediately, don’t worry! Walk past it tomorrow, and you might find your target.



I spent 20 minutes waiting for indigo buntings yesterday, and today they just sit on the trail.








Read more about the colorful nine-primaried oscines: Why Are Buntings All So Good? - Audubon





3. Different birds have different preferences for privacy.
You always see robins, starlings, corvids, pigeons and doves, sparrows, and finches on the open ground. They are braver than other birds, and they usually allow you to approach them closer.



Fluffy chipping sparrow with a rufous-colored hat.


Wrens like to hide in the bushes. You need to bow to see them, and those birds fly away as soon as you stare at them for too long.
Waxwings, mockingbirds, thrashers, cardinals, and catbirds sometimes jump on the branches of roadside shrubs. They are braver than many other birds, but if you approach them suddenly, they will certainly fly away.
Pewees, vireos, and orioles are very shy. They usually skulk in the canopy of large trees, and most times you can only identify them by their songs.



Baltimore oriole were not named after the city Baltimore; rather, they were named after the flag of Lord Baltimore because of their black-and-yellow plumage. You can also see that color from the famous Maryland flag. It’s almost 30 meters from me to this beautiful little oriole bird.








Read more about niche partitioning, the classic ecology concept: Spruce-Woods Warblers Revisited: 60 Years Later, the Cast of Characters Has Changed - Cornell Lab





4. Stand still, and use your Dynamic Visual Acuity to find them.
That’s it. Use your DVA. If you find a ‘singing’ tree, stand still under it and wait for 15 minutes, it’s highly likely that you’ll find that singing bird.



Due to their camouflage, it’s almost impossible to find this little vireo with your naked eyes - unless you see it flying to a branch.




5. Size and vibe matter.
Size and vibe of a bird really matter when trying to identify it in the wild.
For example, people often confuse orioles with robins, since they both have a darker back and a bright orange belly; but if you know that orioles are smaller, and robins like to walk with their heads held high and chests out, you’ll be able to differentiate them immediately. American goldfinches like to fly in pairs, if you see some little lemon-yellow bullets flying up and down while glittering under the sun, that’s them!



Comparing to their Chinese relatives spotted doves which chase and bow to the female birds every 5 seconds in mating seasons, mourning doves look calm and demure, and you can see that from their silhouette.


Sometimes you can see large waterfowl and raptors flying overhead, and it’s possible to identify them only by the way they fly. For example, double-crested cormorants fly by flapping their wings really fast, and if you see some huge bird with its neck retracted, that’s almost always a great blue heron.






Read more about the birds’ ‘vibe’: Identifying Birds with GISS or JIZZ - Ornithology, the Science of Birds
crumbs: Birding｜Summertime: Watching Songbirds in Your Favourite Park

title: Birding｜Summertime: Watching Songbirds in Your Favourite Park
text:
Some Memories
Three days ago, for the first time, I saw a female red-winged blackbird. She was an incredibly cute little bird, with facial features that subtly mirrored her male counterpart. She was diligently pulling algae from the pond. I initially thought I was seeing some kind of American dipper or waterthrush. After discussing with my friends, we confirmed that it’s not a new lifer, which was a bit of a disappointment. Then I remembered her mate flying nearby, calling out loudly. Okay, who am I to stop the happy couple from being there?



Unlike its male counterpart, the female red-winged blackbird does not have those striking red-and-white epaulettes. This one likes washing herself.


I also heard some gray catbirds meowing, which reminded me of two summers I’d spent on the East Coast before. These light and fluffy gray birds always evoked memories of summer. They are braver birds, slightly smaller than a robin, and like their relatives, mockingbirds, they can mock other birds’ songs. Someone called it ‘buzz-cut bird’ - okay, that’s fair - but I’d like to call it ‘nun bird’ since I think that small patch of gray feathers on its head looks like a nun’s hat.



My little meow meow… with these little claws…


Additionally, I saw a common nighthawk flying overhead, with two prominent white patches on its wings. It flew very high; I initially thought it was a chimney swift. In China, we have nightjars - nighthawks’ relatives - which have a mating call that resembles a laser gun. The American version does not sound like that. In ancient China, nightjars were called ‘mosquito mother’ because of their massive gapes, and the ancients believed that mosquitoes were spat out by them.
Speaking of which, I got bitten four times by mosquitoes that day. Even fully covered, going into the woods always comes at a price. The good thing is that we don’t have Aedes here. Back in my hometown, I have got blisters all over my legs because of Aedes bites, and trust me, that’s an absolute nightmare.

title: Birding｜Summertime: Watching Songbirds in Your Favourite Park
section: The Reason We Need a Scientific Name
text:
The Reason We Need a Scientific Name
If you’re a Chinese birder like me, you might also be fascinated by the New World birds’ beautiful feathers while easily get confused by their common names.
What do you mean by ‘indigo bunting is indeed a cardinal’? Why are ‘new world sparrows’ indeed ‘old world buntings’? Why are American robins look like our Chinese blackbirds, as they both walk that way and like pulling earthworms from the ground? Is Beatles singing about our red-winged blackbird in their White album? - that would be a very, very loud song.

Baltimore orioles and red-winged blackbirds are both New World Blackbirds (Icterids), which has no relationship with our Old World Blackbirds (Turdus, aka thrushes).
Indigo bunting, as well as summer tanager and scarlet tanager, are not buntings (Emberizidae, aka old world buntings) nor tanagers (Thraupidae, mostly neotropical birds) but indeed cardinals as our friend northern cardinal (Cardinalidae).
American robin is a thrush (Turdus), like Chinese blackbird. It has nothing to do with European robin (Muscicapidae, aka Old World Flycatchers).
Paul McCartney was singing about European blackbirds/common blackbirds, which look exactly like Chinese blackbirds. Read this interesting article: Does a Blackbird Sing in a Beatles’ Song?
Speaking of new world sparrows and old world buntings, this reply on the iNaturalist forum answers it perfectly:


’The “new world sparrows”, Passerellidae, are part of a radiation of birds that happened in north and south america over the last ~17 million years or so, named the Emberizoidea.
The common ancestor of Emberizoidea probably started in the Americas, but early on, one lineage went back to Eurasia and formed the ancestor of the old world buntings (Emberizidae) and the longspurs (Calcariidae). Meanwhile, the group continued to diversify in the Americas, forming the new world tanagers, sparrows, warblers, cardinals, and a bunch of smaller families.
The closest relatives of the Paserelidae sparrows are the new world warblers, blackbirds, and some smaller lineages endemic to the Caribbean and Central America (eg. chat-tanager, wrenthrush, Puerto Rican tanager, Spindalis).
So, in the grand scheme of things, the Passerellidae are fairly closely related to the Emberizidae (both in Emberizoidea), though they are not each other’s closest relatives (Emberizidae is closer to the longspurs, Paserellidae is closer to new world warblers/cardinals/tanagers/etc.
The Passeridae sparrows are even more distantly related: the common ancestor of the Passeridae and Emberizoidea probably lived in Eurasia a little over 20 million years ago. After Passeridae split off, that lineage did not produce any other families, so technically the Emberizoidea are their closest relatives, but so are the Fringillidae finches and Motacillidae wagtails that branched off before Emberizoidea started to radiate into its different families.’

title: Who Is The Saddest Shoegaze Band?
text:
1 Introduction

1.1 Why This Project
I’m interested in the ‘shoegaze’ subgenre of indie rock. This less-known genre, also called ‘the scene that celebrates itself’, rose from the noise pop scene in the late 80s and early 90s, and has regained popularity recently. An article titled ‘The Shoegaze Revival Hit Its Stride in 2023’1 by pitchfork also captures the revival of shoegaze among GenZ populations.





My bloody valentine’s 1988 EP ‘You made me realise’ is a classic shoegaze record.


Shoegaze is characterized by heavy use of overdriven guitar and various effect pedals with the combination of the ethereal vocals; the lyrics are often regarded as blank, poetic, and sometimes difficult to distinguish from the instruments. So here comes this project for the indieheads - I want to analyze those usually overlooked lyrics, especially from the perspective of sentiment.
The bands I want to study are the so-called classic ‘big-three’ of shoegaze: my bloody valentine, Ride, and slowdive. They were all on the independent record label Creation from London, UK, reached their peak in early 90s, disbanded in late 90s due to the fading of the subgenre, and reunited in the 21st century, which make them a perfect fit to study the changes in the lyrics over the years.


1.2 My Questions

What words frequently appear in their lyrics?
Which bands have the longest and shortest lyrics?
Who is the saddest shoegaze band?
Are bands trending towards happiness or sadness over time?

title: Who Is The Saddest Shoegaze Band?
text:
2 Project

2.1 Data Acquisition & Wrangling


  

2.1.1 Data Acquisition
Lyrics from all studio albums of the ‘big three’ bands in the shoegaze genre - my bloody valentine (mbv), Ride, and slowdive - are retrieved from Genius.com using a Python package named lyricsgenius2 based on Genius API. Please see the author’s instructions for details.






The downloaded .json files were written into a .csv file for further processing. Please go to the source repository for more details.




# load packages
library('stringi')
library('tidyverse')
library('lubridate')
library('knitr')

# reference
knitr::write_bib("rmarkdown", file = "my-refs.bib")

# import data
lyrics <- read.csv("data/lyrics_data.csv")
kable(head(lyrics, n = 1))

Song.Title
Artist
Release.Date
Lyrics
Album.Name

Soft as velvet, eyes can’t see Bring me close to ecstasy High away to heaven, and I’m coming too Float now, coming down on me (Ooh, ooh) Handed you what I cannot see (Ooh, ooh) Feel the big happy, you’re exploding me (Ooh, ooh) Soft as snow and warm inside (Ooh ooh) Penetrate then re-divide (Ooh, ooh) Slip away forever, really need you (Ooh, ooh) You might also like Ooh, ooh Ooh, ooh Ooh, ooh Ooh, ooh Ooh, ooh Ooh, ooh Ooh, ooh Ooh, ooh1Embed

2.1.2 Data Dictionary








Field Name
Data Type
Description

The lyrics of the song


Album.Name

2.1.3 Data Wrangling
The lyrics directly retrieved from Genius.com usually have some problems -







‘16 ContributorsBallad of Sister Sue Lyrics’ at the beginning and ‘6Embed’ at the end are not part of the lyrics.
‘√¢¬Ä¬ô’ - some problem with Unicode encoding/decoding.
‘See Slowdive LiveGet tickets as low as $55’ - ads is also not part of the lyrics.




So, it requires some data cleaning.

# clean text
lyrics_clean <- lyrics %>%
  mutate(Lyrics = stri_enc_toutf8(Lyrics)) %>%
  mutate(Lyrics = str_replace_all(Lyrics, 'â\u0080\u0099', "'")) %>%
  mutate(
    Lyrics = Lyrics %>%
      str_remove(".*Lyrics") %>%
      str_remove("See.*tickets as low as \\$\\d+") %>%
      str_remove('You might also like') %>%
      str_remove('\\d*\\s*Embed$') %>%
      str_trim()
  ) %>%
  rename(Album = Album.Name) %>%
  filter(!str_detect(Lyrics, "^\\s*$")) # filter out instrumental pieces

# add some factors for further processing
lyrics_clean <- lyrics_clean %>%
  mutate(lyric.length = nchar(Lyrics),
         Release.Date = dmy(Release.Date),
         Release.Year = year(Release.Date))

print(lyrics_clean[1,'Lyrics'])

[1] "Soft as snow but warm inside Penetrate, you cannot hide Feeling lost forever, really need you Feeling dark and feeling true This is all I ever knew Soft as skin in leather and I whisper, \"You\" Harder you come down on me (Ooh, ooh) Sink away, you look happy (Ooh, ooh) Secrets keep forever, they're undressing me (Ooh, ooh) Come inside, it's warm in here (Ooh, ooh) Better now to have no fear (Ooh, ooh) Carried on a wave, where it can lead you? (Ooh, ooh) Touch your head, then your hair Softer, softer everywhere Fingertips are burning, can I touch you there? Soft as velvet, eyes can't see Bring me close to ecstasy High away to heaven, and I'm coming too Float now, coming down on me (Ooh, ooh) Handed you what I cannot see (Ooh, ooh) Feel the big happy, you're exploding me (Ooh, ooh) Soft as snow and warm inside (Ooh ooh) Penetrate then re-divide (Ooh, ooh) Slip away forever, really need you (Ooh, ooh)  Ooh, ooh Ooh, ooh Ooh, ooh Ooh, ooh Ooh, ooh Ooh, ooh Ooh, ooh Ooh, ooh"

# this is for ride-only analysis
lyrics_ride <- lyrics_clean %>%
  filter(Artist == 'Ride')

# this keeps the dataset working for the original analysis
lyrics_clean <- lyrics_clean %>%
  filter(!str_detect(Album, "\\[EP\\]")) %>%
  mutate(Album = factor(Album, 
                        levels = c("Isn’t Anything", "loveless", "m b v", 
                                   "Nowhere", "Going Blank Again", "Carnival of Light", "Tarantula", "Weather Diaries", "This Is Not a Safe Place", "Interplay", 
                                   "Just for a Day", "Souvlaki", "Pygmalion", "Slowdive", "​​​everything is alive")))




2.2 Data Analysis

2.2.1 What words frequently appear in their lyrics?

library('tidytext')

# tokenize by word
token <- lyrics_clean %>%
  unnest_tokens(output = Word,
                input = Lyrics,
                token = 'words')

# stopwords dropped
token_clean <- token %>%
  anti_join(stop_words, by = c("Word" = "word"))

token_count_cloud <- token_clean %>%
  group_by(Artist) %>%
  count(Word, name = 'Word_count', sort = TRUE)

token_count_head <- token_count_cloud %>%
  group_by(Artist) %>%
  slice(1:30) %>%
  mutate(Word = fct_reorder(Word, Word_count, .desc = FALSE))

# make a word cloud
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw())
library(ggwordcloud)
palette <- c(
  "my bloody valentine" = "#d83c7a",
  "Ride" = "#4b8ab8",
  "Slowdive" = "#ae8f32",
  "when you sleep" = "#f576a8",
  "Vapour Trail" = "#56a8e3",
  "When the Sun Hits" = "#d1b971"
  )

ggplot(token_count_head, aes(
  label = Word,
  size = Word_count,
  color = Artist
)) +
  geom_text_wordcloud(word.ratio = 0.2, # adjust for overall word size
                      max_size = 30) +
  facet_wrap(~ Artist) +
  scale_color_manual(values = palette) +
  labs(
    title = 'Most Frequently Used Words in Lyrics',
    caption = 'Word size based on frequency. Only the top 30 results are shown here.'
  )








The result is kind of amusing. Ride and mbv rely their vocals heavily on harmonies and hummings - and it’s reflected honestly here, while slowdive has the most ‘meaningful’ lyrics among the three. ‘Love’ is the ultimate meaning of rock and roll, and it indeed appears in high frequency in all of their lyrics.


2.2.2 Which bands have the longest and shortest lyrics?

# plotting
ggplot(lyrics_clean, aes(x = Album, y = lyric.length, fill = Artist)) + 
  geom_boxplot(color = 'black') +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette) +
  labs(
    title = 'Which bands have the Longest/Shortest Lyrics?',
    caption = 'Boxplot showing the range and median of lyric lengths for each Album.', 
    color = 'Before Reunion?', 
    y = 'Lyric Length (character)'
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))








Among the three bands, Mbv always has the shortest lyrics overall while Ride has the longest. An interesting trend is that while Ride and slowdive have similar lyric length back in the 90s, after reunion, Ride tends to have longer lyrics - and the length increases for each album.


2.2.3 Who is the saddest shoegaze band?
I used afinn from package tidytext for sentiment analysis based on this paper3.

# data processing: sentiment 'afinn'
token_count <- token_clean %>%
  group_by(Artist, Album, Release.Year) %>%
  count(Word, name = 'Word_count', sort = TRUE) %>%
  ungroup()

token_afinn <- token_count %>%
  inner_join(get_sentiments('afinn'), by = c("Word" = "word"))

afinn_score_by_artist <- token_afinn %>%
  group_by(Artist) %>%
  summarize(avg = round(mean(value), 2)) %>%
  ungroup()

kable(afinn_score_by_artist)




Artist
avg




Ride
-0.06


Slowdive
0.00


my bloody valentine
-0.11





Among the three bands, mbv has the lowest sentiment score, which means it is the saddest shoegaze band (if we only look at the lyrics). All three bands got sentiment scores less than or equal to zero, with slowdive holding the highest score (0.00).

2.2.3.1 What about their greatest hits?
Using data from last.fm, we find out that the greatest hits of the three bands are:

when you sleep - my bloody valentine (32171 weekly listeners),
Vapour Trail - Ride (1943 weekly listeners), and
When the Sun Hits - Slowdive (53055 weekly listeners).

I’m interested that whether those songs have a happier or sadder vibe compared to their other songs -

# by song
token_count_bysong <- token_clean %>%
  group_by(Artist, Song.Title) %>%
  count(Word, name = 'Word_count', sort = TRUE) %>%
  ungroup()

# give afinn score
token_afinn_bysong <- token_count_bysong %>%
  inner_join(get_sentiments('afinn'), by = c("Word" = "word"))

# clean data set, drop songs with only 1/2 rows
token_afinn_bysong <- token_afinn_bysong %>%
  group_by(Song.Title) %>%
  filter(n() > 2) %>%
  ungroup()

# calculate average scores
afinn_score_all <- token_afinn_bysong %>%
  group_by(Song.Title, Artist) %>%
  summarize(avg_song = mean(value))

# look at the greatest hits
afinn_score_gh <- afinn_score_all %>%
  filter(Song.Title == 'Vapour Trail' | Song.Title == 'When the Sun Hits' | Song.Title == 'when you sleep')

# combine datasets for plotting
afinn_score_gh <- inner_join(afinn_score_gh, afinn_score_by_artist, by = c("Artist" = "Artist"))

# plot
ggplot(afinn_score_gh, aes(x = Artist)) +
  geom_point(shape = 16, size = 3, aes(y = afinn_score_gh$avg, color = Artist)) +
  geom_point(shape = 17, size = 3, aes(y = afinn_score_gh$avg_song, color = 
Song.Title)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = palette) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = 'black') +
  labs(
    title = 'Who is the Saddest Shoegaze Band?',
    caption = 'Average sentiment score calculated based on afinn scores.\n<0: sad/negative, >0: happy/positive.', 
    y = 'Sentiment Score', 
    x = 'Time', 
    color = 'Artist average/\ngreatest hits'
  )








Mbv has the lowest overall sentiment score. All those songs have a slightly higher sentiment score than their artist’s average scores. People seem to prefer happy songs!


2.2.3.2 So what are their happiest/saddest songs?

extreme_song <- afinn_score_all %>%
  group_by(Artist) %>%
  filter(avg_song == max(avg_song) | avg_song == min(avg_song)) %>%
  ungroup()

sorted_tibble <- extreme_song %>%
  group_by(Artist) %>%
  arrange(Artist, avg_song) %>%
  ungroup()

kable(sorted_tibble)




Song.Title
Artist
avg_song




I Came to See the Wreck
Ride
-1.500000


Only Now
Ride
-1.500000


The Dawn Patrol
Ride
2.000000


The Sadman
Slowdive
-2.333333


Everyone Knows
Slowdive
3.000000


if i am
my bloody valentine
-1.400000


only shallow
my bloody valentine
2.000000





With the table above, we find that Ride’s saddest songs are ‘I Came to See the Wreck’ and ‘Only Now’, and happiest songs is ‘The Dawn Patrol’; Slowdive’s saddest song is ‘The Sadman’, and happiest songs is ‘Everyone Knows’; mbv’s saddest song is ‘if i am’, and happiest song is ‘only shallow’. The Sadman is really sad.



2.2.4 Are bands trending towards happiness or sadness over time?

afinn_score <- token_afinn %>%
  group_by(Artist, Album, Release.Year) %>%
  summarize(avg = mean(value))

library(ggrepel)
ggplot(afinn_score,
       aes(x = Release.Year, y = avg, color = Artist, label = Album)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  geom_text_repel(size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = 'black') +
  scale_color_manual(values = palette) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-1,1)) +
  labs(
    title = 'Sentiment Trend of Lyrics Over Time',
    caption = 'Average sentiment score calculated based on afinn scores.\n<0: sad/negative, >0: happy/positive.',
    color = 'Artist',
    y = 'Sentiment Score', 
    x = 'Time'
  )








When examining the trend over time, it is noteworthy that at the beginning of their careers, the bands all had very sad lyrics; in the middle of their careers, their lyrics became more positive. It is also interesting to observe that the latest albums of mbv, Ride, and Slowdive are all among the saddest of their entire careers.

title: Who Is The Saddest Shoegaze Band?
section: 3 Bonus: Here Comes the RIDE Fan!
text:
3 Bonus: Here Comes the RIDE Fan!
RIDE blew my mind when I attended their Nowhere concert with the Charlatans back in Jan 2024 in the amazing venue Union Transfer, Philadelphia. Since then I’ve become a huge fan… So I couldn’t help but did more data analysis on them (!).
Disclaimer: I’m by no means overlooking the members who do not write the lyrics. I love you Steve. It’s just because I can only do text analysis at this time.

3.1 My Questions

Who writes the lyrics in each album?
What’s the most frequently used words for each lyricist before/after reunion?
Top 5 Words for Each Album
Who is the Saddest Lyricist?
Are they trending towards happiness or sadness over time?



3.2 Data Wrangling
Information about lyric writers were from interviews and record sleeves.

# assign lyricist
andy_bell_songs <- c("Drive Blind", "Close My Eyes", "Like A Daydream", "Silver", "Dreams Burn Down", "Here And Now", "Seagull", "Kaleidoscope", "In a Different Place", "Polar Bear", "Paralysed", "Vapour Trail", "Sennen", "Beneath", "Today", "Not Fazed", "Chrome Waves", "Time of Her Time", "Cool Your Boots", "Making Judy Smile", "Going Blank Again", "Howard Hughes", "Birdman", "Crown of Creation", "Endless Road", "Magical Spring", "I Don’t Know Where It Comes From", "Sunshine/Nowhere To Run", "Dead Man", "Walk on Water", "Mary Anne", "Castle On The Hill", "Gonna Be Alright", "The Dawn Patrol", "Ride The Wind", "Burnin’", "Starlight Motel", "Charm Assault", "Home Is A Feeling", "Weather Diaries", "Lateral Alice", "Cali", "Impermanence","Cold Water People", "Catch You Dreaming", "Future Love", "Repetition", "Kill Switch", "Clouds of Saint Marie", "Fifteen Minutes", "Jump Jet", "Dial Up", "End Game", "In This Room", "Peace Sign", "Last Frontier", "Light in a Quiet Room", "Stay Free", "Last Night I Went Somewhere to Dream", "Midnight Rider", "Portland Rocks", "Yesterday Is Just a Song")

mark_gardener_songs <- c("Chelsea Girl", "All I Can See", "Furthest Sense", "Perfect Time", "Taste", "Decay", "Unfamiliar", "Leave Them All Behind", "Twisterella", "Mouse Trap", "Time Machine", "OX4", "Stampede", "Moonlight Medicine", "1000 Miles", "From Time To Time", "Only Now", "Deep Inside My Pocket", "Lannoy Point", "White Sands", "Pulsar", "Keep It Surreal", "Shadows Behind the Sun", "Monaco", "I Came to See the Wreck", "Sunrise Chaser", "Essaouira")

loz_colbert_songs <- c("Nowhere", "Natural Grace", "Rocket Silver Symphony", "R.I.D.E.")

collab_songs <- c("All I Want", "Eternal Recurrence")

cover_songs <- c("How Does It Feel to Feel?")

lyrics_ride <- lyrics_ride %>%
  mutate(lyricist = case_when(
         Song.Title %in% andy_bell_songs ~ "Andy.Bell",
         Song.Title %in% mark_gardener_songs ~ "Mark.Gardener",
         Song.Title %in% loz_colbert_songs ~ "Loz.Colbert",
         Song.Title %in% collab_songs ~ "collaboration",
         Song.Title %in% cover_songs ~ "cover",
         TRUE ~ NA_character_
         ),
         Album = fct_reorder(Album, Release.Date),
         is90 = Release.Year < 2000)



3.3 Data Analysis

# tokenize
# tokenize by word
ride_token <- lyrics_ride %>%
  unnest_tokens(output = Word,
                input = Lyrics,
                token = 'words')

# unique by song
ride_token_unique <- ride_token %>%
  group_by(Song.Title) %>%
  distinct(Song.Title, Word, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  ungroup()

# stopwords dropped
ride_token_clean <- ride_token_unique %>%
  anti_join(stop_words, by = c("Word" = "word"))


3.3.1 Who writes the lyrics in each album?

# who writes what
ggplot(lyrics_ride, aes(x = Album, fill = lyricist)) +
geom_bar() +
scale_fill_manual(values = ride_palette) +
scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:12, minor_breaks = 1:12) +
theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))+
  labs(title = 'Who writes the lyrics in each album?',
    fill = 'Lyricist',
    y = 'Count', 
    x = 'Album'
  )








Andy Bell did a lot, especially for Nowhere, Tarantula, and This is Not a Safe Place.


3.3.2 What’s the most frequently used words for each lyricist before/after reunion?

# count - lyricist, is90
ride_token_count <- ride_token_clean %>%
  group_by(lyricist, is90) %>%
  count(Word, name = 'Word_count', sort = TRUE) %>% 
  ungroup()

# find top 15
ride_token_count_head_bylyricist <- ride_token_count %>%
  group_by(lyricist, is90) %>%
  filter(lyricist == 'Andy.Bell' | lyricist == 'Mark.Gardener') %>%
  slice(1:15) %>%
  mutate(Word = fct_reorder(Word, Word_count, .desc = FALSE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# most frequent words
ggplot(ride_token_count_head_bylyricist, aes(x = Word_count, y = Word, fill = is90)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap( ~ lyricist) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ride_palette, name = 'Status', labels = c('After Reunion', 'Before Reunion')) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25), minor_breaks = 1:25) +
  labs(title = "What's the most frequently used words for each lyricist\nbefore/after reunion?",
    fill = 'Before Reunion',
    caption = 'Only top 15 frequently used words were shown.',
    y = 'Word', 
    x = 'Count'
  )








It’s surprising that ‘time’ was used a lot. I’m interested that whether all bands like this word or it’s just RIDE. Maybe it would be my next project in the future.


3.3.3 Top 5 Words for Each Album

# The Word for each album?
ride_token_count_album <- ride_token_clean %>%
  group_by(Album) %>%
  count(Word, name = 'Word_count', sort = TRUE)

# find top 5
ride_token_count_album_head <- ride_token_count_album %>%
  group_by(Album) %>%
  slice(1:5) %>%
  filter(!Word_count == 1) %>%
  mutate(Word = fct_reorder(Word, Word_count, .desc = FALSE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# plotting
ggplot(ride_token_count_album_head, aes(x = Album, y = Word, label = Word)) +
  geom_text(size = 3, aes(color = Word_count)) +
  scale_color_continuous(high = '#a688b9', low = '#ccd8e0') +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 0.3) + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = 'Top 5 Words for Each Album',
    color = 'Count',
    y = 'Word', 
    x = 'Album'
  )








Some themes are always there - time, day, life, feel…


3.3.4 Who is the Saddest Lyricist?

# who is more depressed
ride_token_count_aa <- ride_token_clean %>%
  group_by(lyricist, Album, Release.Date) %>%
  count(Word, name = 'Word_count', sort = TRUE) %>%
  ungroup()

# apply sentiment value
ride_token_afinn_aa <- ride_token_count_aa %>%
  inner_join(get_sentiments('afinn'), by = c("Word" = "word")) %>% 
  filter(lyricist == 'Mark.Gardener' | lyricist == 'Andy.Bell' | lyricist == 'Loz.Colbert')

# calculate overall score
ride_afinn_score_by_lyricist <- ride_token_afinn_aa %>%
  group_by(lyricist) %>%
  summarize(weighted_avg = round(sum(value * Word_count) / sum(Word_count),2)) %>%
  ungroup()

# plotting
ggplot(ride_afinn_score_by_lyricist, aes(x = lyricist, y = weighted_avg, fill = lyricist, label = weighted_avg)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(-1, 0, 1), limits = c(-1.5,1.5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ride_palette) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = 'black') +
  labs(title = 'Who is the Saddest Lyricist?',
    y = 'Sentiment Score', 
    caption = 'Average sentiment score calculated based on afinn scores.\n<0: sad/negative, >0: happy/positive.',
    x = 'Lyricist',
    fill = 'Lyricist'
  )








Mark Gardener seems really sad.


3.3.5 Are they trending towards happiness or sadness over time?

# Is anyone getting more depressed over time?
# assign affin score for each person for each album
ride_afinn_score_by_lyricist_album <- ride_token_afinn_aa %>%
  group_by(lyricist, Album, Release.Date) %>%
  summarize(weighted_avg = round(sum(value * Word_count) / sum(Word_count),2))

# geom_line() must work with numeric factor
ride_afinn_score_by_lyricist_album$Album_num <- as.numeric(ride_afinn_score_by_lyricist_album$Album)

# plotting
ggplot(ride_afinn_score_by_lyricist_album, 
       aes(x = Album_num, y = weighted_avg, color = lyricist, shape = lyricist, label = Album)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) + 
  geom_line() +
  scale_color_manual(values = ride_palette) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = ride_afinn_score_by_lyricist_album$Album_num,
    labels = ride_afinn_score_by_lyricist_album$Album
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-2,2)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = 'black') +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = 'Sentiment Trend of Lyrics Over Time',
    caption = 'Average sentiment score calculated based on afinn scores.\n<0: sad/negative, >0: happy/positive.',
    color = 'lyricist',
    y = 'Sentiment Score', 
    x = 'Album'
  )








Are people getting sadder when they get old?
